native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (ever_jailed = 1, determined by residence in jail or detention facilities between 1985 and 1994) have significantly lower wealth compared to those without in all three examined years (1985, 1990, and 1996) based on unconditional parametric (Welch's t-test, p < 0.001) and non-parametric tests (Mann-Whitney U test, p < 0.001). In multivariate econometric regressions controlling for race and sex, the wealth deficit is statistically significant in 1990 and 1996 under classical OLS (p < 0.01), and statistically significant across all years (1985, 1990, and 1996) when utilizing heteroscedasticity-robust HC3 standard errors and median quantile regressions, with the magnitude of the wealth penalty widening substantially from 1985 to 1996.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Inspected data structure, verified complete absence of missing records across 12,013 observations in NLSY79 data. 2. Computed group-level summary statistics (mean, median, standard deviation, IQR) by incarceration status (ever_jailed) across 1985, 1990, and 1996 composite wealth. 3. Conducted two-sample Welch t-tests and Mann-Whitney U rank-sum tests for each year. 4. Estimated multivariate OLS regression models controlling for race and sex with classical and HC3 robust standard errors. 5. Estimated median quantile regressions and pooled panel regressions with interaction terms (ever_jailed x year) to quantify the widening intertemporal wealth gap.
